core_obligations: Forward direction: obtain flatness of F over O from flatness of F' via the change-of-rings lemma, and injectivity of I tensor_O F -> F' by tensoring F' with the exact sequence 0 -> I -> O' -> O -> 0 and applying the vanishing of Tor over a flat module (proof lines 5018-5027).

Converse, set-up: for an injective map alpha of O'-modules, introduce the subsheaves of sections annihilated by I and record that K tensor_{O'} F' = K tensor_O F for any O'-module K annihilated by I (proof lines 5028-5033).

Converse, main step: examine the displayed commutative diagram of tensor products along 0 -> G -> G' -> G'/G -> 0 and deduce injectivity of the middle vertical map from the two outer ones, using the hypothesis on I tensor_O F -> F' for the outer terms (proof lines 5034-5055).
proof_roadmap: Derive the forward direction from change of rings and the Tor vanishing criterion.
For the converse, filter an arbitrary injection along the I-torsion subsheaf.
Conclude injectivity of the induced map on tensor products.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes flatness of a module over a square-zero thickening O' -> O in terms of the flatness of its reduction F = F'/I F' over O together with injectivity of the multiplication map I tensor_O F -> F'. The forward direction uses stability of flatness under the change of rings O' -> O and applies the tensor product by F' to the defining exact sequence, invoking the vanishing of Tor for flat modules (proof lines 5018-5027). The converse is the substantive direction: it takes an injective map of O'-modules, cuts it along the subsheaves annihilated by I, and works with the resulting commutative diagram, using throughout that tensoring an O'-module annihilated by I agrees with tensoring over O (proof lines 5028-5055). H2: the diagram chase along the I-torsion filtration of the injection is the substance and is written out.
